userStories.title: Native turn blocking, prompt context and handler deadlines
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] runNativeTurn with a registered before_turn handler returning { block: { reason: "no secrets in prompts" } } rejects with a NaxError whose code is NATIVE_TURN_BLOCKED and whose message is no secrets in prompts.
[unit] In that blocked runNativeTurn, the fake provider complete dependency is never called.
[unit] After that blocked runNativeTurn on a session seeded with one prior exchange, the session's transcript holds exactly the prior exchange's messages: the blocked prompt is not persisted.

[unit] runNativeTurn with prompt fix it and a before_turn handler returning { promptContext: "branch: main" } sends the provider a final user message whose content is branch: main

fix it.

[unit] runNativeTurn with prompt look, one image attachment in opts.images and a before_turn handler returning { promptContext: "ctx" } sends a final user message with content ctx

look that still carries that image.
[unit] runNativeTurn with a before_turn handler returning { promptContext: "" } sends the prompt message content unchanged.

[unit] runNativeTurn with a before_turn handler returning both { seed: [{ role: "user", content: "seeded" }], promptContext: "ctx" } sends a user message whose content is ctx

seeded.
[unit] runNativeTurn with a before_turn handler returning both block and promptContext rejects with NATIVE_TURN_BLOCKED: block wins.

[unit] createLoopEventRegistry().dispatch("before_turn", payload) returns all four fields unchanged when its registered handler returns { seed: [{ role: "user", content: "seeded" }], history: [{ role: "user", content: "prior" }], block: { reason: "deny" }, promptContext: "x" }.

[unit] wrapExternalHandler for an entry with timeoutMs: 50 whose handler never settles answers a before_tool dispatch with a block outcome after the 50 ms deadline, while _externalHandlerDeps.timeoutMs is set to 10000.

[unit] wrapExternalHandler for an entry with timeoutMs: 5000 whose before_tool handler settles { kind: "allow" } after 100 ms answers allow, while _externalHandlerDeps.timeoutMs is set to 20: the entry's deadline replaces the default.
[unit] wrapExternalHandler for an entry with no timeoutMs whose handler never settles answers block once _externalHandlerDeps.timeoutMs (set to 30) elapses.

[unit] wrapExternalHandler for an entry with timeoutMs: 0, and for one with timeoutMs: Infinity, whose handler never settles answers block once _externalHandlerDeps.timeoutMs (set to 30) elapses: only a finite positive timeoutMs replaces the default.

[unit] When an external before_turn handler fails to settle within its timeoutMs, wrapExternalHandler returns an empty patch, leaving the event unchanged as required by the existing wrapper failure rule.

routing.reasoning: Four existing modules receive additive type fields, a helper-level turn check/prefix and a deadline fallback using established patterns; session and prompt-blocking boundaries still require the strict security/session strategy.

suggestedCriteria: runNativeTurn rejection for a block patch carries error context { stage: "native-session", sessionName: handle.id }.
wrapExternalHandler falls back to _externalHandlerDeps.timeoutMs for negative or NaN entry.timeoutMs values.

userStories.title: Deliver session, prompt and stop hooks
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Extend createAgentHookHandlers with first-turn context, prompt guard/context and bounded stop continuations.

**Motivation** — A user who wants "run prettier after every edit", "never let the agent `git push`" or "keep going until the tests pass" has to write a plugin.

**Approach** — Extend the existing factory, not a separate registration mechanism. `SessionStart` maps to `before_turn` when the turn's loaded `history` is empty. `UserPromptSubmit` maps to `before_turn` every turn, after `SessionStart` hooks. `Stop` maps to `before_turn_end` when the turn ended `"completed"` and not by a stop.

**Deadline.** Each factory handler's `timeoutMs` is `AGENT_HOOK_HANDLER_MARGIN_MS + Σ (entry.timeoutMs + AGENT_HOOK_KILL_GRACE_MS + AGENT_HOOK_DRAIN_MS)` over the entries that handler may run on its surface (for `before_turn`: every `SessionStart` and `UserPromptSubmit` entry, whether or not `SessionStart` runs on a given turn). The constants live in `run-hook.ts`: `AGENT_HOOK_KILL_GRACE_MS = 5000` (SIGTERM to SIGKILL), `AGENT_HOOK_DRAIN_MS = 2000` (stream drain bound), `AGENT_HOOK_HANDLER_MARGIN_MS = 1000`. With this bound a hook always reports its own timeout or error before the wrapper's deadline fires, so the per-event failure rules below, not the wrapper's generic ones, decide the outcome.

**Combining several entries of one event** (one handler runs them all, in config order):
- Context strings (`additionalContext`, and plain-text stdout where it counts as context) are joined with `"\n\n"` in entry order; empty strings are dropped.
- `UserPromptSubmit`: the first block stops the remaining `UserPromptSubmit` entries and the handler returns only `block`.
- `Stop`: the first block stops the remaining `Stop` entries.
- A JSON-object stdout is never treated as plain text: a `SessionStart` entry answering `{}` adds no context.
- A JSON `decision: "block"` without a string `reason` uses the reason `blocked by hook '<command>'`.

stdin JSON (every event): `hook_event_name`, `session_id` (the context's `sessionName`), `cwd`, `surface` (`"chat"` | `"run"`), and, when the context has them, `role`, `feature`, `story_id`, `model`. Per event:
- `UserPromptSubmit`: `prompt`.
- `SessionStart`: no extra field.
- `Stop`: `stop_hook_active` (true when `followUpsSoFar > 0`, i.e. from the second `Stop` run of a turn on). The loop's existing cap (`MAX_FOLLOW_UPS_PER_TURN = 3`) still applies: a hook that always blocks makes the agent continue at most 3 times per turn.

For `UserPromptSubmit` and `SessionStart` a plain-text stdout on exit 0 is context. Read `decision` (`"block"`), `reason`, `additionalContext` for UserPromptSubmit; `additionalContext` for SessionStart; `decision` (`"block"`) and `reason` for Stop. SessionStart exit-2 block is ignored with a warning. Hook errors: `UserPromptSubmit` blocks the prompt on `chat` and is let through with a warning on `run`; `SessionStart`, `Stop` log a warning and change nothing. Explicit UserPromptSubmit blocks apply on both surfaces and discard accumulated context. An empty result returns undefined, not a fabricated context patch. Reuse factory scope filtering, cwd/common payload and runner seam from US-004; run all applicable SessionStart entries before UserPromptSubmit.

The producer seam is `BeforeTurnPatch.block` and `promptContext` from US-001. The handler returns those patches and does not replace prompt messages with seed. The stop producer returns `{ followUp: reason }` and relies on the existing loop cap, never bypasses it.

**Scope** — In: extending handlers.ts and adding turn-handlers.test.ts. Out: native loop consumers/deadline wrapper (US-001), tool-handler semantics (US-004), surface loader/chat (US-006), run setup (US-007). 
- Shell hooks on the other loop events (`transform_context`, `before_request`, `after_response`, `before_compaction`).
- Concatenating `before_turn` `seed` or `promptContext` patches across several handlers; `dispatchChain` keeps overwrite semantics, so a later plugin handler returning `promptContext` replaces the agent hooks' value.

**Interface** — Extend this same factory without changing its signature:
```typescript
export function createAgentHookHandlers(input: {
  readonly config: AgentHooksConfig;
  readonly surface: AgentHookSurface;
  readonly repoRoot: string;
}): LoopHandlerSet;
```
Return `BeforeTurnPatch` with `readonly block?: { readonly reason: string }` / `readonly promptContext?: string`, or `BeforeTurnEndPatch` with `readonly followUp?: string`, through the existing ExternalHandlerOf loop contract.
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] With one SessionStart entry of timeoutMs 1000 and one UserPromptSubmit entry of timeoutMs 2000 on surface chat, createAgentHookHandlers returns exactly one before_turn entry with timeoutMs 18000 (1000 + (1000 + 7000) + (2000 + 7000)).
[unit] With one Stop entry of timeoutMs 3000, createAgentHookHandlers returns one before_turn_end entry with timeoutMs 11000.

[unit] The before_turn handler for a payload with empty history runs the SessionStart entry with hook_event_name: "SessionStart", then the UserPromptSubmit entry with hook_event_name: "UserPromptSubmit" and prompt = the payload's prompt, in that order.
[unit] The before_turn handler for a payload with non-empty history does not run the SessionStart entry.

[unit] A SessionStart run of { kind: "ok", stdout: "repo: nax" } and a UserPromptSubmit run answering json { additionalContext: "be brief" } make the handler return { promptContext: "repo: nax\n\nbe brief" }.
[unit] A UserPromptSubmit run of { kind: "ok", stdout: "today is monday" } (plain text) makes the handler return { promptContext: "today is monday" }.
[unit] A SessionStart run of kind: "ok" with json {} and a UserPromptSubmit run of { kind: "ok", stdout: "" } make the handler return undefined.
[unit] A UserPromptSubmit run of { kind: "block", reason: "contains a key" } returns { block: { reason: "contains a key" } } with no promptContext, and a later UserPromptSubmit entry is not run.
[unit] A UserPromptSubmit run of kind: "ok" with json { decision: "block", reason: "r" } returns { block: { reason: "r" } }.
[unit] On surface chat, a UserPromptSubmit run of { kind: "error", reason: "exited 3" } returns a block whose reason names the entry's command and exited 3.
[unit] On surface run, a UserPromptSubmit run of { kind: "error", reason: "exited 3" } returns no block, the next UserPromptSubmit entry still runs, and one warning names the command.
[unit] A SessionStart run of kind: "block" or kind: "error" adds no context and no block, and logs one warning.
[unit] The before_turn_end handler for { ended: "completed", stopped: false, followUpsSoFar: 0 } runs the Stop entry with hook_event_name: "Stop" and stop_hook_active: false.
[unit] For followUpsSoFar: 1 the Stop payload carries stop_hook_active: true.
[unit] A Stop run of { kind: "block", reason: "tests still fail" } makes the handler return { followUp: "tests still fail" }, and a later Stop entry is not run.
[unit] A Stop run of kind: "ok" with json { decision: "block", reason: "go on" } returns { followUp: "go on" }.
[unit] A Stop run of { kind: "ok", stdout: "" } returns undefined.
[unit] A Stop run of kind: "error" returns undefined and logs one warning naming the command.
[unit] The before_turn_end handler runs no Stop entry for ended: "aborted", for ended: "errored", or for ended: "completed" with stopped: true.

routing.reasoning: Extends the upstream factory in one source module with two handlers reusing its runner, filtering and deadline conventions; prompt blocking and session-first-turn decisions require strict security/session TDD.

suggestedCriteria: On either surface, a JSON UserPromptSubmit block without a string reason returns a block reason of blocked by hook '<command>'.
When a Stop JSON block has no string reason, before_turn_end returns followUp equal to blocked by hook '<command>'.
When a first-turn prompt is blocked and loaded history remains empty on the next turn, the next before_turn dispatch runs SessionStart again.
When a Stop hook always blocks, a native turn honors no more than three followUp continuations.
When one context-producing entry answers an empty string between two non-empty contexts, the final promptContext contains only the two non-empty texts separated by one blank line.

userStories.title: Load hook handlers once and append them to chat resources
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Add the non-throwing handler loader and connect chat resources to the factory through an injectable dependency.

**Motivation** — The run lifecycle hooks in `hooks.json` (`on-start`, `on-story-complete`, ...) are shell commands, but they fire only in `nax run`, only on run lifecycle events, and cannot block or change anything.

**Approach** — `loadAgentHookHandlers` reads `<repoRoot>/.nax` and `globalConfigDir()` through `_loadAgentHookDeps` and returns `createAgentHookHandlers(...)`. It never rejects: an unexpected throw from loading yields an empty set and one `agent-hooks` warning, so a broken `hooks.json` never stops chat or a run.

`chatResources` (`packages/nax/src/cli/chat.ts`)
- Baseline: `pluginHandlers: registry.getLoopHandlers()`
- Target: `pluginHandlers: [...registry.getLoopHandlers(), ...(await deps.loadAgentHookHandlers({ surface: "chat", repoRoot }))]`, with `loadAgentHookHandlers` added to `_chatCommandDeps`.

**Ordering at the wiring sites.** On both surfaces the order is plugin handlers, then agent hooks, then rule delivery: chat appends the agent-hook handlers to `pluginHandlers` and `ChatHost` appends rule delivery after them; run passes `[...pluginHandlers, ...agentHooks]` into `withRuleDeliveryHandlers`, which appends rule delivery last (the existing "rules after plugins" rule). Rule delivery answers `before_tool` with a nudge (read) or a block (write) and `dispatchBeforeTool` keeps only the last nudge, so for a call where both answer a nudge, the rule text wins (see Out of Scope).

**Subagents.** Chat subagents inherit `ChatHost.loopHandlers`, so chat-scoped agent hooks also run inside chat subagent turns.

Barrel: each story adds its new module's exports to `packages/nax/src/hooks/agent/index.ts` (created by US-002), and `packages/nax/src/hooks/index.ts` re-exports them; `cli/chat.ts` and `run-rules-setup.ts` import from `@/hooks`, never from an internal file.

Read the config once during chat startup, not on each turn. Use the existing chat entry trust gate; runner trust rechecks remain in US-003. Do not change ChatHost's later existing host-job guards, resource teardown, ACP behavior or the package-declared-hooks notice. The native-only loop forwarding and subagent inheritance already exist and need no alternate path.

**Scope** — In: load.ts and its barrel exports, _chatCommandDeps and chatResources integration, unit loader tests and chatCommand seam integration assertions. Out: handler behavior (US-004/005), run/bot opt-in wiring (US-007).
- Reloading `hooks.json` during a chat or run; the config is read once when the surface starts.
- Agent hooks for ACP brains (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor as the chat agent); they run their own hooks and loop handlers reach only the native agent.
- Executing Claude Code's own hooks (`~/.claude/settings.json`, plugin `hooks.json`) or package-declared hooks listed by `packages/nax/src/resources/parse-hooks.ts`; the chat notice that they are not executed stays.
- Merging a hook's `PreToolUse` nudge with rule delivery's nudge for the same call; the later handler's nudge wins (rule delivery, on both surfaces).

**Interface** —
```typescript
// load.ts
export const _loadAgentHookDeps: { loadAgentHooksConfig: typeof loadAgentHooksConfig; globalDir: () => string };
export function loadAgentHookHandlers(input: {
  readonly surface: AgentHookSurface;
  readonly repoRoot: string;
}): Promise<LoopHandlerSet>;
```
acceptanceCriteria: [unit] loadAgentHookHandlers({ surface: "run", repoRoot }) calls the stubbed _loadAgentHookDeps.loadAgentHooksConfig with join(repoRoot, ".nax") and the stubbed _loadAgentHookDeps.globalDir() value.
[unit] loadAgentHookHandlers given a stubbed config with one PreToolUse entry scoped ["run"] returns one before_tool entry for surface run and an empty set for surface chat.
[unit] loadAgentHookHandlers whose stubbed loadAgentHooksConfig rejects resolves to an empty set.
[unit] loadAgentHookHandlers whose stubbed loadAgentHooksConfig rejects logs one agent-hooks warning.

[integration] loadAgentHookHandlers imported from @/hooks, called with surface: "run" and a temp repo whose .nax/hooks.json holds one Stop entry and an empty global directory, returns one before_turn_end entry with plugin agent-hooks.
[integration] chatCommand with _chatCommandDeps.loadAgentHookHandlers stubbed to return one sentinel entry calls the stub once with { surface: "chat", repoRoot }.

[integration] chatCommand with _chatCommandDeps.loadAgentHookHandlers stubbed to return one sentinel entry passes resources to the stubbed createChatHost whose pluginHandlers end with that sentinel entry after the plugin registry's entries.
[integration] chatCommand with loadAgentHookHandlers stubbed to return an empty set creates the host with pluginHandlers equal to the plugin registry's entries.

routing.reasoning: Loader/barrel and chat dependency wiring are standard, but activate repository-controlled hooks in interactive sessions; strict security/session isolation is retained.

suggestedCriteria: When _loadAgentHookDeps.globalDir throws, loadAgentHookHandlers resolves to an empty set with one agent-hooks warning.
When chatCommand's trust gate refuses the project, loadAgentHookHandlers is never called.
When chat launches native subagents, their loop-handler set includes the same chat-scoped agent-hook entry objects received by the parent ChatHost.

userStories.title: Opt run into agent hooks without enabling bot worktrees
userStories.description:
**Goal** — Load run-scoped agent hooks only through an explicit shared-setup opt-in while preserving rules ordering, validation and empty-set identity.

**Motivation** — The only way to influence a native-agent tool call today is an in-process JavaScript plugin providing `loop-handlers`.

**Approach** — `configureRunRules` (`packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-rules-setup.ts`)
- Baseline: `configureRunRules(input: { config; workdir; pluginHandlers }): Promise<LoopHandlerSet>` returning `withRuleDeliveryHandlers(...)`
- Target: input gains optional `agentHooks?: "run"`. [...input.pluginHandlers, ...hooks] : input.pluginHandlers`, so rule delivery stays last. When `agentHooks` is absent the loader is not called. `initializeAfterLock` (`packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-init.ts`)
- Baseline: `configureRunRules({ config, workdir, pluginHandlers: pluginRegistry.getLoopHandlers() })`
- Target: the same call plus `agentHooks: "run"`.

**Bot is excluded.** `packages/nax/src/bot/run-setup.ts` also calls `configureRunRules`, on a PR worktree that may come from a fork. Agent hooks are therefore opt-in on `configureRunRules` (`agentHooks: "run"`), passed only by `initializeAfterLock` (`packages/nax/src/execution/lifecycle/run-setup-init.ts`); the bot call stays as it is and loads no agent hooks.

**Ordering at the wiring sites.** On both surfaces the order is plugin handlers, then agent hooks, then rule delivery: chat appends the agent-hook handlers to `pluginHandlers` and `ChatHost` appends rule delivery after them; run passes `[...pluginHandlers, ...agentHooks]` into `withRuleDeliveryHandlers`, which appends rule delivery last (the existing "rules after plugins" rule). Rule delivery answers `before_tool` with a nudge (read) or a block (write) and `dispatchBeforeTool` keeps only the last nudge, so for a call where both answer a nudge, the rule text wins (see Out of Scope).

Retain all current overrideDir/project-context validation before invoking the hook loader: a missing overrideDir still throws RULES_OVERRIDE_DIR_NOT_FOUND without loading hooks. Invoke the loader when opted in even when rule delivery is skipped; workflow mode and rule-delivery settings gate rule delivery, not agent hooks. When hooks are empty or opt-in absent, preserve the exact plugin set by identity wherever existing withRuleDeliveryHandlers does. Import the loader from @/hooks.
